findings.claim: IsPublicReadWrite's field branch is inverted: it uses `field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst`. Ordinary public mutable fields (`public int X;`) are never serialized in contractless mode. Public `readonly` fields are treated as read-write (CreateMember hardcodes IsWritable: true), so the generated Deserialize assigns to a readonly field and the generated code fails with CS0191.

Run Contractless_PublicReadonlyField_DoesNotBreakCompilation: the output compilation has a CS0191 error in generated code.

findings.claim: When no SurrogateType is set, the collector always goes contractless (CreateContractlessMembers) and never reads [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] (or [DataContract]/[DataMember]) on T. An [IgnoreMember] public property of an attributed T is still serialized, and [Key(int)] array layout is replaced by string-key map mode. This violates the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterCollectorLogicTests.AttributedType_IgnoreMember_IsHonoured: the generated user formatter text contains 'SecretXyz' although that member is [IgnoreMember].

findings.claim: needsCast compares m.Name against "OnBeforeSerialize"/"OnAfterDeserialize" for explicit interface implementations. The metadata name of an explicit implementation is 'MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize', so needsCast is always false. For a T that implements the callback receiver explicitly, the template emits `value.OnBeforeSerialize()` without the cast, and the generated code does not compile (CS1061). The check also only inspects T's own members, not base types.

findings.claim: IsPartial only checks the formatter's own declaration. A [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class nested inside a non-partial containing class passes validation. The template then wraps the body in EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces (re-declaring the outer class), which yields CS0260 (missing partial modifier) instead of a MsgPack019 diagnostic.

findings.claim: The generated-formatter model is added to modelPerType alongside the regular TypeCollector models with no deduplication by DataType. When T is also a [MessagePackObject] type in the same compilation, the resolver gets two ObjectSerializationInfo entries for the same data type. This risks a duplicate key in the resolver's type lookup (TypeInitializationException at run time) or a duplicate registration.
